statement: A school club sells tickets to a show for $\$30$ each. The payment service keeps $5\%$ of every ticket sale as a fee. The club needs to keep at least $\$2{,}400$ after the fee. What is the least number of tickets the club must sell?

choices.misconception: I took $5\%$ off the $2{,}400$ dollar goal instead of off each ticket, so I divided $2{,}280$ by $30$ and got $76$.
I divided $2{,}400$ by $30$ and ignored the fee, so I got $80$ tickets.
I added $5\%$ to the goal to cover the fee, which gave $2{,}520$, and divided by $30$ to get $84$, but $5\%$ of the larger sales is more than $120$ dollars.

hints: Find how much the club keeps from one ticket.
The club keeps $95\%$ of each $30$ dollar sale. Write an inequality for the amount kept and solve it, then round to a whole number of tickets.
The club keeps $0.95 \cdot 30 = 28.50$ dollars per ticket, so solve $28.50n \ge 2{,}400$.

solutions.reliable: From each ticket the club keeps $0.95 \cdot 30 = 28.50$ dollars. It needs $28.50n \ge 2{,}400$, so $n \ge 84.21...$. The least whole number is $85$. Check: $85$ tickets keep $85 \cdot 28.50 = 2{,}422.50$ dollars, while $84$ tickets keep only $2{,}394$ dollars.
